data.exact_reserve_text: During 2014 the net loss ratio (net of acquisitions costs) on certain lines of business for the 2012 and prior years of account was increased. These increases are set out in the table below together with their effect on ultimate claims reserves.
data.standardized_narrative: The Syndicate strengthened prior year reserves by GBP 23.342m (approximately 8.37% of opening gross claims outstanding), driven by increases to the Liability (Casualty) and Treaty portfolios relating to 2012 and prior years. The movement was described as an increase in the net loss ratio on certain 2012 & prior years of account, with the largest uplift in the Liability book.
raw_causal_phrases: During 2014 the net loss ratio (net of acquisitions costs) on certain lines of business for the 2012 and prior years of account was increased.
The result was affected by worse than expected claims experienced primarily in the US liability account and further movement in the discontinued element of the Treaty account.

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: Opening gross claims outstanding taken from Balance Sheet (Claims outstanding, comparative column 2013). Prior year development derived from Note 'Movement in prior year's provision for claims outstanding' which quantifies increases in claims reserves for Treaty and Liability (shown as insurance liabilities increases in GBP 000). No gross claims development triangle was found in the provided text to cross-check; figures in Note 5 are explicit gross reserve increases and treated as authoritative.
